text.en: In school Asha attended a health talk. "Healthy habits protect us from harm," said the counsellor.

Health means being well in body, mind and society. This chapter explains abuse and how to protect oneself: any harm to a child by an adult is abuse, and children should know safe and unsafe behaviour, trust a parent or teacher, and report to the helpline when something is wrong.
Drug abuse is the wrong use of drugs, alcohol and tobacco. It leads to dependence, behavioural changes and harm to the body. Tobacco smoking causes lung disease and cancer. Alcohol harms the liver and the brain. De-addiction and rehabilitation measures with medical help and family support help people recover.
The chapter also lists common diseases and their prevention, and stresses healthy habits like clean food, exercise and avoiding addictive substances.

problem.en: Whom can a child tell if someone makes them feel unsafe?

text.en: A parent, a teacher or a helpline can help.
So tell a trusted adult at once.

prompt.en: A friend says Smoking is harmless in small amounts. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Tobacco harms the lungs and heart.

points.en: Health covers body, mind and society.
Tell a trusted adult if unsafe.
Tobacco and alcohol harm the body.
